exact_goal: For every finite group G of order n and every word a_1,...,a_(2n-1), there are i_1<...<i_n with a_(i_1)...a_(i_n)=1.

claims.statement: For every nonzero odd natural m, Mathlib DihedralGroup m has cardinality2m; the list r^(2m-1) followed by s^(2m-1) has length2|G|-2; every ordered sublist of length|G| has product different from1.
claims.scope: partial: one-short lower-bound family, not the conjecture at length2|G|-1
assumptions: Mathlib's actual dihedral group and List.Sublist
claims.novelty: Reproduces the odd-dihedral bound already claimed in Agarwal–Lou2016 abstract; no novelty claim; their full proof not recovered
claims.verification: lake env lean accepted; axioms printed; parent Comparator replay is independent and not claimed here

claims.statement: If |G|=n, orders of a,b are p,q, their cyclic subgroups intersect trivially and lcm(p,q)=n, then a^(n-1)b^(n-1) has no ordered n-term identity product, whereas a^(n-1)c b^(n-1) does for every c in G.
assumptions: lcm of generator orders equals group order
claims.novelty: Not established; elementary observation, no novelty claim

claims.statement: Two180-second exact SMT searches on A4 and C3 semidirect C4 each returned UNKNOWN/timeout. No counterexample and no exclusion certificate was obtained.
claims.verification: Both tables' group axioms checked; semidirect one-short SAT witness raw-enumerated; fixed identity extension UNSAT control
